name: Bermuda
summary_text: Bermuda is a British Overseas Territory. Local legislation governs, and the United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex services code do not automatically extend to Bermuda; United Kingdom measures could be applied only by Order in Council.  The House of Assembly voted 22–16 on 14 May 1994 to decriminalise consensual sex between adult men, striking two sections of the Criminal Code. The debate divided the island, with religious leaders split and the Christian Coalition staging marches against the change.  In July 2013 the Senate passed the Human Rights Amendment Act, which outlawed discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and, in the same instrument, on grounds of age. Same-sex marriage was not permitted at that point.  The Governor gave assent to the Domestic Partnership Act in February 2018. It replaced same-sex marriage with domestic partnerships open to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples, making Bermuda the first jurisdiction to revoke marriage equality. Recognition of a same-sex partner therefore rests on the partnership register rather than on marriage.

sources.title: Criminal Code - Stubbs Bill 1994 and 1 November 2019 amendment; gross indecency repeal
sources.documents: Legal status of homosexual activity; 1994 legalization of consensual conduct in private with unequal age of consent 18 vs 16; 2019 reform setting 18 for anal intercourse and repealing gross indecency between men
sources.detail: No URL shown in text. Cited as: Prior to 1994 anal/oral sex punishable up to ten years; Stubbs Bill 1994; violation of European Convention on Human Rights; law took effect 1 November 2019; as of 2022 age still not equal
